title: Entropy per unit of energy, at one frequency
spoken: At fixed frequency, the partial derivative of the spectral entropy density with respect to the spectral energy density is one over the temperature.
explanation: At equilibrium, moving a little energy from one frequency interval to another gains no entropy to first order, so this derivative has one common value across the spectrum. The thermodynamic identity dS/dE = 1/T names that value.
assumptions: Radiation in equilibrium at fixed volume.
Entropy density and energy density are compared at one frequency.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed paper. The paper writes phi for the entropy density.

notes.title: Rate of change at fixed frequency
notes.explanation: How much the entropy density rises per unit of added energy density, with the frequency held where it is.

notes.title: One over the temperature
notes.explanation: Thermodynamics defines temperature this way: dS/dE = 1/T, with the other constraints fixed.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: At equilibrium every frequency interval gains the same entropy per unit of energy, and that common value is 1/T.

notes.title: Spectral energy density
notes.explanation: Radiation energy per cubic metre per unit of frequency.

notes.title: Spectral entropy density
notes.explanation: Entropy per cubic metre per unit of frequency; the paper writes it phi.

notes.title: Frequency, held fixed
notes.explanation: The comparison is made at one frequency; only the energy density changes.

notes.title: Temperature
notes.explanation: The temperature of the radiation in equilibrium.
